3.  Rental Transportation Permit Renewals
  Upon an audit of Vehicle Rental Permits, it was found seven permits had been issued to
  organizations with active business licenses but expired vehicle rental permits.
  Recommended Action
  Approve the renewal of Rental Transportation Permits for Brown’s Bikes, Catalina E
  Bikes, Catalina Business Enterprises, Inc., Catalina Island Company, and Island Rentals,
  Inc. with stated conditions.

4.  First Reading of an Ordinance Amending Title 4, Chapter 4, Article 17 Vehicle
  Registration
  City staff have seen an increase in applications and approvals for commercial autoettes,
  commercial rental autoettes, interior commercial vehicles, and public service/public
  health and safety vehicles. With the increase of permits, it is recommended to add a
  requirement to mark permitted vehicles as an added condition.
  Recommended Action
  Introduce and waive all future readings of an ordinance amending Title 4, Chapter 4,
  Article 17 adding the requirement to mark all commercial autoettes, commercial rental
  autoettes, commercial vehicles, interior commercial vehicles, and public service/public
  health and safety vehicles with the legal name or fictitious business name of the applicant.

5.  Public Transportation Services REP Contract Award
  Utilizing a new fleet of zero emission, all electric vehicles, the City’s goal with the new
  public transportation program is to improve wayfinding, and alleviate congestion and
  demand for on street parking in Avalon’s “downtown” area. The City’s RFP broadly
  requested proposers re-design the transit program to better align with the needs and
  expectations of our community of residents and visitors.
  Recommended Action
  1. Award a contract to Circuit Transit, Inc. for Public Transportation Services; 2. Authorize
  the City Manager to negotiate contract terms. The final contract will be brought before the
  City Council for final consideration and approval.

6.  Authorize Professional Services Contract to Assess the Condition of the Avalon
  Wastewater Treatment Plant
  A task on the City’s Wastewater Treatment Plant Capital Improvement List is to evaluate
  the condition of the plant and complete a list of necessary improvements.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a professional services contract to
  assess the condition of the Avalon Wastewater Treatment Plant for a not to exceed
  amount of $80,000.

SUBJECT:  Waterside Project Application  —  Newport Coastal Adventure LLC

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): City Council make the finding that Newport Coastal Adventure
LLC will have a substantial negative impact upon existing mooring, docking, or other
anchorage facilities within Avalon Harbor. As Harbor Master it is of my opinion that the addition
of Newport Coastal Adventure to Avalon Harbor will have a substantial negative impact and
increase harbor traffic congestion, and limit available dock space on cruise ship days.

REPORT SUMMARY: The applicant has submitted a Waterside Project Application to offer
sightseeing, whale and dolphin watching trips using a 48’ vessel. The applicant is specifically
interested in providing sightseeing trips on Cruise ship days.

Newport Coastal Adventure LLC proposes the use of a 48’ Rigid Hull Inflatable to conduct
coastal whale and dolphin watching trips in the Avalon area. Newport Coastal Adventure
proposes to operate on cruise ship days, up to 4 days a week, from January 1, to December
31, and between the hours of 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. The vessel will obtain a mooring from
Avalon Harbor Patrol as needed.

In my opinion as Avalon Harbor Master, the project will not result in any substantial negative
impact upon Avalon Harbor, except as noted in subsection (2), below.

Section 10-2.416 of the Municipal Code provides that a waterside permit may only be granted
where the City Council is able to make the following affirmative findings:

  (1)  The project will not result in a substantial alteration of the City’s present or
planned waterside uses of the Avalon Harbor;

  (2)  With regard to transportation and circulation, the project (I) will not generate
  substantial additional boat trips, including shoreboat trips, or other movement
  within Avalon Harbor;

In my opinion as Harbor Master the project will generate substantial additional boat trips, or
other movement within Avalon Harbor because without mitigation by applicant and without
additional dock space available for use on Cruise Ship days, existing permit holders and the
public will be negatively impacted.
   (ii) Will not have a substantial negative impact upon existing mooring, docking,
  or other anchorage facilities,’

In my opinion as Harbor Master the project will have substantial negative impact upon docking
and other facilities because without mitigation by applicant and without additional dock space
available for use on Cruise Ship days, existing permit holders and the public will be negatively
impacted.
  (iii) Will not have a substantial impact on other modes and systems of
  transportation;

In my opinion as Harbor Master the project will have substantial impact on other modes and
systems of transportation because without mitigation by applicant and without additional dock
space available for use on Cruise Ship days, existing permit holders and the public will be
negatively impacted.

  (iv) Will not result in substantial alterations of present patterns of circulation or
  movement of people and/or goods;

In my opinion as Harbor Master the project will result in substantial alterations of present
patterns of circulation or movement of people and br goods because without mitigation by
applicant and without additional dock space available for use on Cruise Ship days, existing
permit holders and the public will be negatively impacted,;

  (vi) Will not restrict or alter existing coastal access;

In my opinion as Harbor Master the project will alter existing coastal access because without
mitigation by applicant and without additional dock space available for use on Cruise Ship
days, existing permit holders and the public will be negatively impacted.

  (3)  The project will not have a substantial impact upon, and will not result in, a need
for new or altered governmental services, including but not limited to fire, police, maintenance
of facilities, and harbor department services;

This finding cannot be made because the pleasure Pier floats see heavy usage in the summer
months and on cruise ship days, by a mix of charter vessels, dive boats, tour boats, parasail
boats, water taxis, and other users including private boats and additional public services will be
needed if this use is permitted.

  (4)  The project will not result in the use of substantial amounts of fuel or other forms
of energy or substantially increase the demand upon existing energy or require the
development of new sources of energy;

  (5)  The project will not result in the need for new utility systems or a substantial
alteration of existing sources or systems for power, natural gas, communications, water,
sewage disposal or solid waste;
   (6)  The project will not obstruct any scenic vista or view open to the public, and will
not result in the creation of an aesthetically offensive site which is open to public view;

  (7)  The project will not result in a substantial negative impact upon the quality and
quantity of existing recreational opportunities or result in alterations or restrictions to coastal
access;

  (8)  The applicant is fit to be entrusted with the privileges of a permit, in that he has
not engaged in prior violations of the City’s harbor regulations, including the provisions of this
article, has timely paid any harbor-related fees and has not presented checks returned for
insufficient funds.

The Municipal Code also provides that the “City Council may deny the permit where the
impacts listed in paragraphs (1) through (8) above are cumulatively significant, even though
the individual impacts are limited. The City Council may approve a project where mitigation
measures eliminating significant impacts are incorporated into the project, and the approval
shall be conditioned upon the implementation of such mitigation measures. The failure to
comply and maintain any mitigation measures shall be a basis for suspension or revocation of
a waterside permit. Because the findings above cannot be made, Staff recommends the permit
be denied.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Enhance recreational activities in the Avalon Harbor.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Unknown, potential Harbor Use Fees.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Visitors will be able to
use the current operators offering similar services.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Notify Newport Coastal Adventures [[C of the City Council’s decision.

7.8 Fare Revenue Capabilities
Based on the information given in the RFP, a cost savings measure that Circuit
recommends that the City further explores is to utilize adding a fare to the service.
Circuit has experience operating fare-based services throughout many of our
services. Please read below for some insight into why Circuit believes fares can help
to optimize service, and Circuit encourages the City to utilize this option.

In 2021, Circuit implemented a low-cost fare into the Hollywood Sun Shuttle program,
in Hollywood, Florida. The $0 service moved to $1 and Circuit saw the total
ridership continue to grow, despite the increase. Upon further investigation, Circuit
learned that the lack of impact on demand caused by the fare was largely due to the
large increase in TNC (Transportation Network Company) prices in the area. In this
example, the average TNC fare was over 4X higher, for rides starting and ending in
the area. Furthermore, the team found that fares had an impact in reducing
cancellations from riders and therefore led to a more efficient system that moved
more riders. This fare model has worked well and Circuit has regularly reported on
these fares and used them to reduce the cost of the service to the City of Hollywood.

Circuit’s technology includes capability to charge fares on a flat fee basis as well as
dynamic pricing, discount codes, and group rates. We have tested and proven
technology, policies, and programs for offering fare-based programs. Our mobile app
can accept payment via debit, credit, and prepaid cards. The application has the
ability to charge a fee for service and has security in place to store encrypted credit

REPORT SUMMARY: One of the current tasks on the City’s Wastewater Treatment Plant
Capital Improvement List is to evaluate the condition of the plant and complete a list of necessary
improvements. The plant has had several major renovations over the years. These occur on a
regular basis with normal and major maintenance activities. The plant is past fifty years in age
for many of its components. It is subjected to a harsh environment due to its location adjacent
to the ocean and also from the high salinity of the waste stream due to the use of saltwater in
Avalon’s toilets. This harsh environment significantly effects the expected useful life of its
components and therefore the plant requires more extensive maintenance.

As an alternative to the saltwater system, staff previously studied the conversion of the saltwater
system to recycled water which could be used for other uses in addition to the replacement of
toilet water. The recycled water alternative appears very promising as the City already has a
dual water distribution system to each parcel. A major portion of the initial cost on a recycled
water system is the installation of a second distribution system known as “purple pipe” within the
built environment which is impactful to the existing infrastructure such as roadways.

Upon submitting a draft plan to the California Division of Drinking Water it appeared that there
was not a clear path forward with the simple conversion of the existing system to recycled water.
There would likely need to be major revisions of the existing system to satisfy the current
requirements as there were no other dual piped systems in California for residential homes. Yet,
City staff were told that direct potable reuse was on the horizon and to wait for that to develop.
So the study was put on hold. Staff recently received information that direct potable reuse will
be allowed soon.

So there is a renewed interest to evaluate the plant for its renovation, replacement and/or the
ability to reuse the water that is now being sent to the ocean. In addition the conversion to one
water system or an improved water system appears more possible.
 This evaluation is the first step is the process of further studying the alternatives. Grants and
